messages:
Maria: Heads up — brought up reranker v3-int8 on the holdout. NDCG@10 is up ~1.8% but MRR@10 dropped ~3.2%. Strange signal, flagging for triage.
Josh: ugh that gap smells like candidate ordering or tokenization mismatch. any diffs in preproc?
Maria: quick diffs: same candidate set, same sampling. Quant pipeline: PTQ int8 w/ per-channel calibration; eval harness used pytorch dynamic quant in a dev branch.
Kevin: can you paste the eval command you ran?
Maria: sure:
```
# eval command
python -m eval.rerank --model models/v3-int8.pt --candidates candidate_pool.jsonl \
  --queries holdout_queries.jsonl --metric ndcg,mrr --batch-size 64 --seed 42
```
Sophie: did the harness use the same tokenizer & normalizer as prod? small differences cause MRR swings.
Maria: find attached diff in token counts: dev-harness tokenizes avg 38 tokens, prod runtime 36. difference from URL/whitespace stripping.
Josh: that could change tie-breaking. MRR is sensitive to top-1 moves. NDCG can improve if head gets better but tail worsens.
Kevin: also check score scaling after quant. we sometimes see compression toward center. run a quick score-distribution compare:
```
# snippet to dump score hist
python -c "import json, numpy as np; s=json.load(open('scores_dev.json')); print(np.percentile(s, [1,50,99]))"
```
Maria: dumped percentiles. dev v3-int8 scores p1=-0.12 p50=0.02 p99=0.98, prod float p1=-0.5 p50=0.12 p99=1.4. Looks like int8 collapsed the range.
Sophie: that explains it. compressed scores -> more ties -> top-1 more volatile -> MRR down. NDCG can still go up if ranking within top-k improves on average.
Josh: action items: 1) repro with prod tokenizer in eval harness 2) rerun quant with min-max per-channel calibration tweak 3) do an analysis by query length & candidate-count slices.
Kevin: +1. I'll run slice analysis. Would be useful to see per-query delta for top-1 and top-k. small script:
```
# per-query delta
for q in queries:
  top_float = rank(float_model, q)
  top_int = rank(int8_model, q)
  if top_float[0] != top_int[0]:
    print(q.id, top_float[0], top_int[0])
```
Maria: started the re-run with prod tokenizer config now. pinging when done. :eyes:
eval-bot: job_349182 started by Maria — rerun with tokenizer=prod-config, seed=42.
Sophie: also check candidate normalization: do we strip HTML tags consistently? earlier incidents showed embed mismatch when description fields had trailing newlines.
Josh: good call. I can run a quick normalize pass and diff the candidate text hashes.
Maria: re-run finished. results: when using prod tokenizer + html-strip + quant with alternative calibration, MRR drop reduced to -0.4% and NDCG uplift stays +1.2%.
Kevin: promising. can you post per-slice numbers? short queries (<10 tokens) vs long (>50) esp.
Maria: short: NDCG +0.7% MRR -0.6%. long: NDCG +2.6% MRR -0.1%. interesting — long queries benefited more.
Sophie: might be because long queries create richer context for the reranker to discriminate even when scores compress.
Josh: next: add a calibration step to expand score variance after quant (simple affine rescale on logits) and test if that restores MRR without hurting NDCG.
Kevin: if rescale helps, we can bake it into the runtime mapping for int8 models. remember to log that mapping in the model profile.
Maria: running affine rescale alpha=1.8, beta=-0.06 on int8 outputs now.
Maria: results with rescale: MRR delta +0.9% (vs float baseline now MRR -0.1%), NDCG +1.0%. Looks acceptable.
Sophie: please add a small eval note to the model card: quantized-int8-rescale-applied, calibration params, tokenizer=prod-config.
Maria: will update model metadata and trigger canary.
Josh: long-term, we should add a lightweight score-distribution test to the onboarding checklist: ensure p1/p50/p99 within tolerances. saves us future surprises. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Kevin: agree. created issue INF-1427 to add checks + example thresholds.
Maria: thanks team. follow-ups: INF-1427, PR with tokenizer fix, model card update. closing thread unless new regressions. :thumbsup:
